scoring_justification: T1 recompute of invariant reaction types from raw CSV is infeasible because a reliable classification requires a full phase diagram solver; instead we perform a structural audit on the CSV and cross-check the reported JSON against the paper's gold (T0).

hidden_assets.purpose: Gold invariant reaction types for parameter sweep and Cd‑Mg temperatures
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper Table 1 and text (Moser et al 1984 for Cd‑Mg temperatures approximated as 125°C, 186°C, 253°C).
hidden_assets.generation_method: Transcribed from the paper’s Table 1 and the Cd‑Mg section.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are the paper’s actual reported results, used as reference for reproduction scoring.

outputs.description: Raw phase boundary points for all (α,β) parameter sets. The checker recomputes invariant reaction types and Cd-Mg temperatures from this data and compares them to hidden gold values.

items.parameter_sweep: array of objects with alpha, beta, invariant_XB_lt_0.5, invariant_XB_gt_0.5

outputs.description: Agent-reported invariant reaction types and Cd-Mg peritectoid/transition temperatures. The checker compares these directly to hidden paper gold values with tolerant exact match on strings and ±10°C on temperatures.

output_contract.notes: The workflow re-implements the CVM tetrahedron model from published equations; no external data is needed. The agent must produce the solver and run it, not reuse a pre-existing codebase. Phase boundary CSV is the raw artifact from which invariant reactions and temperatures are derived; the checker recomputes the former and cross-checks the latter against the paper-reported table and Cd-Mg values.

steps.description: Verify CSV file contains all required (α,β) parameter sets, has valid columns, and includes plausible phase labels across a range of temperatures.
Compare agent-reported invariant reaction types and Cd‑Mg temperatures to hidden paper gold values with exact string match for invariants and ±10°C tolerance for temperatures.
